messages.content: How much electricity will I need for my 2000 sq ft home?

function.name: solar_panel_calculate_need
function.description: Calculate the number of solar panels needed for a house based on the square footage and average sunlight hours. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

square_footage.description: The square footage of the house. This is a float type value.

average_sunlight_hours.description: The average hours of sunlight received. This is a float type value.

usage_efficiency.description: The efficiency of energy usage in the home, default is 0.8. This is a float type value.

message.content:
A good rule of thumb for a typical U.S. home is **about 5 kWh of electricity per square foot per year**.  
That’s a rough average that covers heating, cooling, lighting, appliances, and electronics for a standard family.

| Metric | Estimate |
|--------|----------|
| **Annual consumption** | 2000 sq ft × 5 kWh/sq ft ≈ **10 000 kWh/year** |
| **Monthly average** | 10 000 kWh ÷ 12 ≈ **833 kWh/month** |
| **Daily average** | 10 000 kWh ÷ 365 ≈ **27 kWh/day** |

### How this breaks down

| Category | Typical % of total | Rough kWh (annual) |
|----------|-------------------|--------------------|
| Heating & cooling | 40–50 % | 4 000–5 000 kWh |
| Lighting | 10–15 % | 1 000–1 500 kWh |
| Appliances (fridge, washer, dryer, etc.) | 20–25 % | 2 000–2 500 kWh |
| Electronics & miscellaneous | 15–20 % | 1 500–2 000 kWh |

> **Note:** These numbers vary widely by climate, insulation quality, HVAC type, appliance efficiency, and lifestyle.  
> • In very hot or cold regions, heating/cooling can dominate and push annual use toward 12 000 kWh or more.  
> • In milder climates or with high‑efficiency HVAC and well‑insulated walls, you might see 8 000–9 000 kWh/year.

### Quick sanity check

If you’re paying about **$0.13 per kWh** (typical U.S. residential rate), your monthly bill would be:

```
833 kWh × $0.13/kWh ≈ $108/month
```

That’s a ballpark figure; your actual bill will depend on your local rate structure, time‑of‑use pricing, and any demand charges.

---

#### Want to see how many solar panels you’d need?

If you’re interested in sizing a solar system, let me know your average daily sunlight hours and I can run the numbers for you.
